hypotheses.claim: The immediate current-G9 parser blocker is predominantly surface/grammar closure rather than absence of a new semantic core primitive.
hypotheses.mechanism: Current source uses control/comparison/optional and prose-like relation spellings not admitted by checked-in grammar; explicit normalization can map them into already expressible call/field/operator structures.
hypotheses.expected_observation: A small core grammar extension plus semantics-conservative normalization closes the full current top-level G9 corpus.
hypotheses.observed: 61/86 baseline -> 86/86 candidate N in executable proxy.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Typed AST construction will reveal that one or more normalized forms encode genuinely distinct semantics requiring a new primitive.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production parser + typed AST oracle cannot preserve intended meaning for one or more failing forms without semantic redesign.
hypotheses.next_test: Production full-corpus parse/typed-AST/roundtrip under matched N/S/D surface policies.

hypotheses.claim: ClayCode should keep source/dialect presentation separable from one deterministic typed canonical IR used for semantic hashing and lowering.
hypotheses.mechanism: Reader-friendly spellings can lower into explicit canonical operations/relations while identity, authority and ordering live in typed IR rather than lexical prose.
hypotheses.support: Fresh full-corpus normalization feasibility plus independent compiler analogues with generic/canonical versus custom assembly forms.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One source surface can directly serve all readers/backends with lower total complexity, making projection layers unnecessary.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched measurements show projection/canonical separation increases repair, latency or semantic drift without compensating determinism or reader gains.
hypotheses.next_test: Measure AST identity, migration edits, tokens, parser complexity, diagnostics and target-reader repair across N/S/D.

hypotheses.claim: Strict normalization (N), @relation sigil (S), and finite declared bare relations (D) are all viable surface policies until compared on the identical complete G9+dialect corpus and typed canonical-IR oracle.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One arm fails full-corpus closure or semantic-hash/diagnostic requirements decisively enough to eliminate it before target-reader testing.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched corpus shows deterministic failure or unsafe semantic admission in an arm.
hypotheses.next_test: Execute the already-revised WORK-CC-BASE-G9-PARSER-FREEZE-001 N/S/D benchmark.
